name: Chronic Intervillositis of Unknown Etiology

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Chronic Intervillositis

criteria.description: Presence of dense mononuclear inflammatory cell infiltrate (primarily histiocytes) in the intervillous space of the placenta
Exclusion of infectious causes by negative microbiological and immunohistochemical studies
Recurrent pregnancy loss, fetal growth restriction, or stillbirth associated with placental pathology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological demonstration of dense intervillous histiocytic infiltrate with exclusion of infectious etiologies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily histopathological; clinical correlation with adverse pregnancy outcomes is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Often presents as multiple miscarriages or stillbirths
Intrauterine growth retardation due to placental insufficiency
searchTerms: baby smaller than expected in womb

pathognomonic.notes: Histological hallmark seen on placental biopsy

common.notes: Mild to moderate platelet count reduction
Increased CRP or ESR in some cases
searchTerms: high inflammation markers in mother's blood

common.symptomName: Abnormal Doppler ultrasound of uterine arteries
searchTerms: abnormal blood flow in uterine arteries

occasional.notes: Presence of antiphospholipid or other autoantibodies in some patients

searchTerms: low red blood cells during pregnancy

occasional.notes: Reduced amniotic fluid volume in some pregnancies

rare.notes: Joint pain without clear inflammatory arthritis
Rarely reported, possibly related to hypertensive complications

laboratory: Presence of maternal autoantibodies (e.g., antiphospholipid antibodies)
imaging: Abnormal uterine artery Doppler velocimetry indicating impaired placental perfusion
Ultrasound evidence of fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible immunogenetic predisposition under investigation
other: Histopathological examination of placenta showing dense intervillous histiocytic infiltrate
Exclusion of infectious agents by microbiological and immunohistochemical studies

distinguishingFeatures: Villitis involves inflammation of chorionic villi rather than intervillous space
Presence of identifiable infectious agents on placental studies
Often accompanied by maternal systemic infection signs
Presence of antiphospholipid antibodies with clinical criteria
Placental infarction and thrombosis rather than predominant intervillous inflammation

redFlags: Recurrent unexplained pregnancy loss or stillbirth
Severe fetal growth restriction with abnormal Doppler studies
Histopathological evidence of dense intervillous inflammatory infiltrate
references: Redline RW. Chronic intervillositis of unknown etiology: a placental lesion associated with recurrent miscarriage and fetal growth restriction. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2007.
Bos M et al. Chronic histiocytic intervillositis: clinical significance and management. Placenta. 2019.
Orphanet: Chronic intervillositis of unknown etiology (ORPHA:615970)
